findings.title: Success-criteria coverage is present at task level
findings.description: At the level of task existence/tracing, no success criterion from the slice design is wholly unrepresented. Functional requirements map as follows: no build/state/detection/`sq` path to 3.3–3.6, 4.1–4.4, 5.1, 6.2 and 6.3; brownfield Phase 0 concept output with no writes to 5.1 and 6.3; byte identity to 2.1–2.2, 3.7 and 6.1; CLI/MCP parity to 5.1; `MIN_GUIDE_VERSION` warning preservation to 3.5, 3.6, 6.1 and 6.3. Technical requirements map to 3.3/6.2 for `services/` imports, 4.1/4.4/6.2 for orphan exports, and 3.7/4.x/6.1 for build/lint/typecheck/tests. The integration requirement that 269 start with no build-path code is implied by the seam-removal and code-gone checks, and the Verification Walkthrough is represented by 6.3. Findings below concern broken checkpoints and check wording, not missing task coverage.

findings.title: Scope, proportionality, test-with pattern and commit-marker mechanics are acceptable
findings.description: The breakdown is one task file, not split into multiple files for a slice of this size. I did not find tasks that should be split or merged: 2.2 and 5.1 are effort 3 but correspond directly to D6 golden capture and D5 purity behavior; 3.3 is large but intentionally grouped because the signature and both callers cannot compile apart. No test task exceeds the success criteria: 2.2 captures the two D6 cases, and 5.1 covers the D5 CLI/MCP/state/`sq`/parity/explicit-key checks. Implementation tasks carry their unit-test edits inline; the D6 baseline is deliberately before source edits; D5 follows the deletion group. No circular dependencies were found; 5.1 uses `git show {target}:.../adoptionParity.test.ts` so it can reuse a deleted test. Non-functional-looking tasks trace to project workflow or explicit design instructions: branch setup to source-control conventions, commit subitems to semantic commits, header/JSDoc/comment rewrites to the Migration Plan and Patterns, and final validation to the success criteria. There are no `**Commit**:` plain-line markers; a file with no markers is acceptable. The checklist commit subitems are distributed through 2.3, 3.2a, 3.7, 4.1–4.4, 5.1 and conditional 6.3, not after every task and not only at the end. The working/tested-point violations are called out in the FAIL finding.

findings.title: No load test or CI gating task is required
findings.description: The slice design restates no NFR, latency, throughput, load, capacity or performance SLO. The task breakdown adds no `tests/load/` task. Under the review rule, absence of a load test and absence of CI gating are not findings because this artifact does not need them; requiring them would be scope creep.

findings.title: 3.2a and 3.7 commit at points where the declared full test suites cannot pass
findings.description: Task 3.2a requires `pnpm --filter @context-forge/core test` to pass before committing the render removal, and task 3.7 requires `pnpm -r test` to pass before committing the seam removal. Those checkpoints occur before `packages/core/tests/adoption/adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts` is deleted in 4.1 and before all brownfield assertions are removed from `packages/core/tests/pipeline-integration.test.ts`. Specifically, `packages/core/tests/adoption/adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts:99-102` still expects `### Adoption Facts`, and `packages/core/tests/pipeline-integration.test.ts:159-188` still expects probe JSON/warnings and a `Comprehension:` line. After 3.1/3.2 remove rendering and 3.3 removes the resolver wiring, those assertions fail; 4.1 deletes `adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts` only after 3.7. This leaves the declared success checkpoints and the Technical Requirement “Format, lint, typecheck and the full test suite pass” unmet at commit points. Fix by moving deletion/rewriting of those tests before 3.2a/3.7, or by narrowing the checkpoint commands to exclude tests that are intentionally updated later.

findings.title: 3.5 CLI test checkpoint lacks the CLI build its integration tests require
findings.description: Task 3.5 requires `pnpm --filter @context-forge/cli test` to pass immediately after source edits. The CLI integration suite spawns `packages/cli/dist/index.js` from `packages/cli/tests/integration/build.integration.test.ts#runBuild`; no `dist/` directory is present in the checkout, and the only earlier build step is `pnpm --filter @context-forge/core build` in 3.4. A junior following the task cannot reliably pass this checkpoint in a fresh checkout. Add `pnpm --filter @context-forge/cli build` or `pnpm -r build` before the CLI test, or defer that CLI integration test to 3.7/6.1 where the full build is already scheduled. This leaves the “full test suite pass” checkpoint in 3.5 ambiguous.

findings.title: Import-grep success checks fail on a retained comment
findings.description: Task 3.3 and 6.2 require `grep -rn "adoption/\|detection/" packages/core/src/services` to print nothing, which is meant to prove the Technical Requirement that `services/` imports nothing from `adoption/` or `detection/`. However `packages/core/src/services/ContextIntegrator.ts:9` currently contains the comment `// contracts.ts only (never adoption/index.ts): keeps services/ and adoption/ from importing each other's internals.` Task 3.3 says to remove imports, but not to delete or rewrite that comment. If the comment survives, the grep prints a line and the declared success criterion cannot be met. Add an explicit comment-cleanup step or narrow the grep to import statements.

findings.title: 6.2 code-gone grep contradicts its own kept `fileComprehension` exception
findings.description: Task 6.2 says `grep -rn "resolveAdoptionFn\|adoptionFacts\|runSquadronProbe\|writeAdoptionState\|fileComprehension\|adoptionStateWrites\|ContextToolOptions" packages/*/src` prints nothing, then immediately allows `COMPREHENSION_PROFILE_VARIABLE = 'fileComprehension'` in `packages/core/src/detection/comprehensionAnalysis.ts:15` to remain. That retained line matches the grep pattern, so “prints nothing” is impossible as written. State the expected exception as one allowed line, exclude that file, or change the pattern so the success check is mechanically achievable.

findings.title: 6.2 export audit can remove symbols the design explicitly keeps
findings.description: Task 6.2’s export audit tells the implementer to accept only symbols with a production consumer listed under the design’s Interfaces Required, or symbols belonging to `history`, `comprehensionAnalysis` or `adoptionOutcome`. That conflicts with kept requirements elsewhere: task context and 4.3 keep `AdoptionError`, `readAdoptionState` and the `ADOPTION_STATES` re-export; the design says `AdoptionError` is still thrown by kept detection modules, and `packages/core/src/introspection/adoptionNavigation.ts:201` consumes `readAdoptionState` until 270. Those consumers are not listed in Interfaces Required. A junior could remove kept exports to satisfy the audit, leaving “No exported symbol remains that only the deleted code used” ambiguous and breaking navigation until 270. Add explicit allowances for the kept symbols and name their consumers.

findings.title: 6.3 walkthrough does not verify concept output with the current CLI output mode
findings.description: Task 6.3 says to run the design’s Verification Walkthrough using `node packages/cli/dist/index.js`, and its success claims the output is the concept prompt with `Adoption Facts` absent. Design step 1 uses `cf build > /tmp/out.md`, but `packages/cli/src/commands/build.ts#registerBuildCommand` writes the context to stdout only in the `--json` branch via `printJson`; the non-JSON branch writes status/help text to stderr and no context to stdout. As written, `/tmp/out.md` can be empty, so the walkthrough does not verify the concept-prompt requirement or the `Adoption Facts` count. Use `cf build --json` and assert on the parsed `.context` field, or adjust the success criterion to name the exact output source.
